note: SAMPLE CONTENT. Hand-written for this demo. Personas are fictional and only inspired by historical figures; no quotes are attributed to real people.
idea: Replace the front desk at a small clinic with a self check-in tablet.

turns.text: Check-in is the same five questions every time. A tablet handles the line at 8 AM without overtime.
An older patient who can't use the tablet gets worse service. A rule that only works for some patients isn't a fair rule.
How does this fail? Insurance cards are wrong, the line backs up anyway, and the desk staff now fix tablet errors.
The tablet can capture details. It can't judge whether someone looks unwell. Keep a person for that.
Let patients check in from their phone before they arrive, and the tablet becomes the backup.
Then the desk shrinks from three people at peak to one greeter who also handles exceptions.
If anyone can still walk up to a person, I can support it.
I'd still pilot it for one month and count the errors before cutting any staff.

recommendation: Offer phone check-in before arrival, keep one greeter at the desk for anyone who wants a person, and use the tablet as backup. Pilot for a month before changing staffing.
dissent: The Skeptic wants the error count from the pilot before any staffing decision.
